 Analysis NFL Week 8 Sunday aftermath: Ravens' season on the brink; can Vikings trust Kyler Murray?
 Published: Updated: Loading... Kevin Patra Senior News Writer Share Facebook Share Twitter Now that it's November, the playoff picture is starting to emerge, and Week 8 featured a number of key divisional matchups that could have lasting effects on the rest of the season.
 The Broncos and Steelers notched revenge wins over the Chiefs and Browns, respectively. The Lions asserted themselves in the uber-tough NFC North, while the Jaguars handed the Colts a potentially fatal blow in a season cratering toward disaster.
 Let's examine some key storylines in Sunday's aftermath, including:
 Another concerning loss for Schottenheimer's 'Boys 
 Minnesota's QB issues rear their ugly head in Detroit 
 Buccaneers lean on run game in historic win 
 Broncos take over driver's seat in AFC West race 
 Burrow channels Norm Van Brocklin against Tennessee 
 But first, we start with Lamar Jackson suffering a potential season-ending injury and where the Ravens go from here.
 Ravens' season on the brink after Jackson injury
 The Baltimore Ravens find themselves in quite the quandary.
 Lamar Jackson's return was supposed to buoy a club coming off back-to-back divisional defeats. It lasted one play on Sunday in Buffalo.
 Jackson’s right thumb injury , which will require surgery, leaves the 4-4 Ravens floundering in the AFC North cellar before we hit Thanksgiving.
 Jesse Minter told reporters after the  36-10 loss to Buffalo that Jackson will be placed on injured reserve, knocking him out for at least four games. Asked if the setback ultimately could end Jackson's season, the Ravens' first-year head coach admitted that it's possible.
 "Potentially, but we'll see where it's at,” Minter said.
 Without the two-time MVP QB, the Ravens' offense is clipped. Baltimore is 7-14 in games in which Jackson has not started since 2019, averaging just 17.6 points. In 2026, the team has scored six touchdowns in the 18 quarters Jackson has missed.
 Jackson’s latest injury shrouds his future in Baltimore. We’ll have plenty of time to delve into the contract situation later. Right now, the focus is on how the Ravens survive.
 It would be bad enough if Jackson's thumb issue were Baltimore's only QB injury, but backup Tyler Huntley also exited Sunday’s game and didn’t return. Minter told reporters Monday that Huntley (toe) probably won't play on  Thursday night against the rolling Jaguars and that the team would "see how it goes from a long-term standpoint."
 Undrafted rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano battled against the Bills, but given the situation -- trying to keep up with Josh Allen on the road with no prep time -- he performed as expected, completing 10 of his 21 pass attempts for 91 yards with a pick and three sacks taken.
 The Ravens are in a rough spot and now on a short week. Even if Huntley doesn’t miss much time, is it worth Baltimore trading for a QB ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline ? Would shelling out more assets in a potentially lost season be wise?
 RELATED CONTENT
 Article 2026 NFL fantasy football waiver wire, Week 9: Jonah Coleman, Mike Washington Jr. top targets about 10 hours ago Article NFL experts' Week 8 takeaways: Do Ravens need drastic QB measures? Plus, Cowboys collapse Nov 01, 2026 Article 2026 NFL season, Week 8: What We Learned from Sunday's games Nov 01, 2026 Let’s rip through some of the potential QB options for the Ravens if they decide to go the trade route.
 Tyson Bagent : The Bears' QB2 struggled in his last outing against Green Bay in  Week 5 and was eventually benched for Case Keenum , but his familiarity with Declan Doyle would benefit Baltimore. Considered one of the league's better backups by many, Bagent could be a long-term play for the Ravens. I have my doubts about if the Bears would be willing to part with their No. 2, but such a move could help recoup some of the  trade capital sent away in last week's Jeffery Simmons deal . The cost to pry Bagent away from Chicago could prove prohibitive for a Ravens team on the brink.
 Jacoby Brissett : Benched in favor of Gardner Minshew during the Cardinals' stirring  comeback win over Dallas on Sunday, Brissett has experience. While inconsistencies have plagued him this season in Arizona, he is a professional QB who could pick up the offense quickly. ( EDITOR'S UPDATE: On Monday, Mike LaFleur named Minshew as the Cardinals' starter "moving forward." ) 
 Shedeur Sanders : Cleveland has insisted that it has no intention of trading Sanders, but coach Todd Monken hasn’t seemed to be in the former Colorado quarterback’s corner at any point in the process. Sanders has his warts, but he could bring more pop to the Ravens' offense than Huntley or Fagnano. The Browns shipped Joe Flacco to Cincinnati last year , so intra-division trades can’t be ruled out. We know the Browns’ brass will take a pick if it makes sense.
 Kirk Cousins : I don’t think the Raiders would trade him while they’re still in contention at 4-4. If they were willing to, the cost would probably be prohibitive. However, for the next week, any QB trade list should at least mention the veteran playing at a high level in front of No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza .
 Two non-trade options:
 Easton Stick : Currently on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad, Stick was in L.A. in 2024 with Minter, so at least there would be some familiarity.
 Jimmy Garoppolo : The veteran hasn’t officially retired. If he wants a shot to play again, Baltimore could be his last best chance.
 Cowboys collapse in stunning loss
 Credit Gardner Minshew for bringing the Mania once again.
 Credit Tyler Allgeier for gashing the Cowboys' defense and powering the Cards back into the game.
 Credit Michael Wilson for continuing to do his best Puka Nacua impression.
 Credit the Cardinals' defense for forcing field goals late and getting a three-and-out in overtime.
 Credit Mike LaFleur’s club for not quitting when quitting could have been easy. And credit the first-year coach for being willing to make a second-half QB change in the heat of the moment.
 Credit the Cards.
 But let’s be real: This was an epic collapse, for which Dallas should be crushed.
 Brian Schottenheimer’s club held a 24-10 fourth-quarter lead before disintegrating like Walter Donovan drinking from the wrong chalice . “He chose poorly” could be the title of every Cowboys move.
 On Sunday, a confluence of ineptitude caused Dallas to collapse at home to drop to 3-5 on the season. The defense became a sieve in the fourth quarter and couldn't tackle. I understand that the Cowboys had some injuries, but letting Allgeier look like Jim Brown is not a product of a few missing players. The secondary inexplicably got burned late when all the Cowboys needed to do was keep everything in front of them. Frankly, Arizona could have scored quicker in the fourth quarter if not for a few misses. The defensive breakdowns continue to perplex Dallas this season. 
 The offense also did its part in the collapse, stalling out inside the red zone early, then failing to get a first down after the Cardinals failed on the onside kick. An explosive offense should be able to move the chains to secure a victory.
 Then there was the depressing three-and-out to begin overtime. Dallas got outgained in yardage 467-261 on Sunday. That should not happen.
 Despite the latest example of Schottenheimer’s teams playing below their talent, Jerry Jones stuck by his coach after the game.
 "That's not in my mind at this time," Jones said when asked about a potential coaching change, per ESPN.com . “... A lot of people let Brian down today, and so, for whatever criticism we want to have of Brian, we can all get in line."
 The line for blame in Dallas is long. It starts at the top.
 Loading... Gregg Rosenthal, Jourdan Rodrigue and Nick Shook recap the Week 8 matchup between the Cardinals and the Cowboys.
 Vikings' QB problems can’t be brushed aside
 Brian Flores' defense had done the heavy lifting to build Minnesota's 6-0 start. But Sunday’s divisional loss to the Lions showed that the ferocious unit can’t do it alone. Detroit went big and ran over the Vikings in the second half, wearing down the stout defense to the tune of 164 rushing yards after halftime. By the end, Flores' group was gassed and couldn’t stop Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions from grinding out the W.
 If the Vikings' offense had any semblance of consistency, the end-game scenario would have played out much differently. Kyler Murray continues to struggle with his consistency. Despite facing the worst passing defense in the NFL on Sunday, he couldn’t keep the Vikings on the field. He sailed more than a few balls way too high, never seemed comfortable and rarely moved the chains. On nine third-down throws, he completed four; three went for first downs.
 Murray connected on some deep balls and averaged 11.2 air yards per attempt, the second-highest mark of his career. But he also missed a host of shots. Per Next Gen Stats, on downfield attempts (10-plus air yards), Murray threw for a season-high 115 yards despite only completing four of his 13 attempts (30.8%), his lowest downfield completion rate in a game since 2023 (min. 10 downfield attempts). The inability to keep the chains moving sits in stark contrast to the best offenses under Kevin O’Connell. We’ll see if KOC pulls the plug and gives  Carson Wentz a shot -- at least we know he’ll force-feed Justin Jefferson -- if the struggles persist.
 The J.J. McCarthy trade probably needed to happen, but seeing the 2024 first-rounder look like a different QB in New York while Murray struggles has to sting Minnesota. 
 With a tough trio of games on tap -- vs. Buffalo (6-1), at Green Bay (5-3) and against San Francisco (6-1) in Mexico City -- the Vikings must get more production from the QB position, or they’ll see their once-strong NFC North lead evaporate.
 EDITOR'S UPDATE: On Monday after publishing, Kevin O’Connell said Kyler Murray is dealing with hamstring tightness . 
 Is the Bucs' offense sustainable?
 The monsoon in Tampa, Fla., dictated the run-heavy approach from Zac Robinson’s offense, but even in pristine weather, the Buccaneers would have leaned on the ground game. The slop tipped the scales even harder, with  Baker Mayfield attempting just three passes -- all falling incomplete -- in the 16-0 win .
 “We knew it was going to be a nasty day and what kind of conditions it was going to be,” Bucs coach Todd Bowles said. “We were worried about ball security and we took care of it other than the fumble in the end zone."
 Bowles added: "I didn’t say we were not going to throw the ball -- the conditions told (Robinson) that. You could see it. It’s a downpour and the wind [was] blowing, you can kind of see the ball wasn’t going anywhere.”
 Tampa became just the second team in the Super Bowl era to have zero completed passes in a single game , joining the 1974 Bills (who did so in a win over the Jets), per NFL Research. Three of the four teams to not have a completion in a game since 1950 have gone on to win, including the Buccaneers on Sunday. They are the first team to win by 10+ points without completing a pass since the 1945 Pittsburgh Steelers beat the Chicago Cardinals.
 The ground game has gotten the Bucs back in the NFC South race. In Week 7 against Carolina , Tampa Bay rushed for 258 yards while Mayfield attempted just 11 passes, completing seven for 64 yards and a TD. Bucky Irving has been sensational, making defenders miss, and has the pop to turn those broken tackles into big runs. All 170 of Irving's rushing yards came after contact on Sunday, per Next Gen Stats .
 One of the more inexplicable issues with the Bucs' early struggles, when they started 1-5, was the offensive line’s play. The veteran crew missed far too many blocks and committed too many penalties. Over the last couple weeks, the group has gotten back on track by smashing defenses in the face. Tampa's rushing attack is absolutely replicable. I expect Irving to keep motoring through defenses, slithering through holes and ripping chunk gains.
 That said, it’s 2026. At some point Mayfield will be asked to win a game through the air. With the Bears and Lions on tap in Weeks 9 and 11, the Bucs will have to keep pace with higher-powered offenses.
 After thumping two division rivals, though, Tampa is back on track in a moribund division. And the Bucs feel like the most stable NFC South club as we head into the second half of the season.
 Loading... Watch the best plays from Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 170-rushing yard, 1 touchdown game vs. the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season.
 Broncos take command in AFC West race 
 It’s not pretty, but who cares when you stack a W?
 Bo Nix earned his 15th career game-winning drive in Denver's 28-24 win over Kansas City on Sunday, breaking a tie with Dak Prescott for the most such drives in a player’s first three seasons since at least 1950, according to NFL Research.
 The Broncos came back to win after trailing the rival Chiefs by 11 points in the fourth quarter. It marked the third victory in Nix’s career in which Denver erased a fourth-quarter deficit of 10+ points, the most such wins in the NFL since 2024.
 Conversely, Sunday marked the third game in Patrick Mahomes ' career in which the Chiefs blew a fourth-quarter lead of 10+ points, and the first since over five years ago, in Week 2 of 2021 at the Ravens.
 Harrison Butker ’s missed fourth-quarter field goal opened the door for Denver, and Nix immediately cashed in, hitting running back Jonah Coleman for a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up the go-ahead 5-yard TD. The 15-point fourth-quarter explosion came after Nix and the offense once again struggled to stay on the field. Denver went three-and-out on three third-quarter drives. Entering the final frame, the home fans were frustrated. Then, boom! Big plays galore, and the Broncos not only escaped with a win but took control of the AFC West race.
 The big plays included a massive goal-line stand by the Denver defense, which held the Chiefs out of the end zone in the game's final seconds after they got a first-and-goal at the 4. The sequence was aided by a K.C. false start, but a Denver D that once again missed too many tackles ultimately stood tall when needed, with Malcolm Roach taking down Mahomes for the game-ending sack .
 “It was ball out or go home,” edge rusher  Que Robinson said of the dramatic finish, via The Denver Post . “And we weren’t going home without that ‘dub.’ ”
 The loss stings K.C., which could have taken complete control of the division race with a sweep over the Broncos. Denver (6-2) has now won four straight, while the Chiefs (5-2) have lost back-to-back games after taking advantage of a soft early slate.
 Andy Reid’s trust in Butker came back to bite him. According to the Next Gen Stats  fourth-down decision guide , with Kansas City leading 24-21 and facing fourth-and-8 from the Broncos' 36-yard line with 2:36 remaining, a punt would have given the Chiefs the highest win probability (74.3%), 1.8 percentage points ahead of going for it (72.5%), while a field goal attempt ranked last (71.5%). Reid elected for the FG. Butker missed the 54-yard attempt, giving the ball back to the Broncos, who scored two plays later.
 Sometimes, analytics does suggest punting.
 Week 8 Sunday spotlight
 Joe Burrow CIN QB Burrow's stat line against the Titans: 38 of 48 (79.2%), 462 yards, 5 TDs, 3 INTs, 115.5 passer rating; 3 rushes, 10 yards, TD 
 Burrow tied a career high with five touchdown passes on 462 passing yards (his third-highest total) and added a go-ahead rushing TD in overtime of the Bengals’ 43-36 victory over the Titans.
 Burrow and Hall of Famer Norm Van Brocklin (against the New York Yankees in Week 1 of the 1951 season) are the only players in league history to have at least 450 passing yards, five touchdown passes and a rushing score in the same game, per NFL Research.
